column3: The Aramaic separately says the king issued a decree and they searched in the house of books where treasures were deposited; BSB combines this as ordering a search of archives in a treasury.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Aramaic repeats King Cyrus as the issuer of the decree; BSB uses “he.”
The Aramaic describes a layer of new timber; BSB says one layer of timbers without “new.” It says “the king’s house”; BSB says “royal treasury.”
The Aramaic ends with an active instruction to deposit the articles; BSB uses the passive “deposited.”
The Aramaic does not separately introduce Darius decreeing, as BSB does. It says “their associates” and names Beyond the River; BSB says “your associates” and specifies west of the Euphrates.
The Aramaic says “its place”; BSB says “its original site.”
The Aramaic names Beyond the River; BSB specifies provinces west of the Euphrates.
The Aramaic repeats day in “day by day”; BSB says “daily.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Aramaic speaks of altering this word; BSB says interfering with this directive.
The Aramaic does not explicitly repeat “this decree” after the verb of altering; BSB supplies it.
The Aramaic names Beyond the River; BSB specifies west of the Euphrates.
The Aramaic has “king of Persia” in the singular; BSB has “kings of Persia” in the plural.
The Aramaic calls the building a house; BSB calls it a temple.
The Aramaic calls them sons of Israel and sons of the exile; BSB says people of Israel and exiles.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls them sons of the exile; BSB says exiles.
The Hebrew leaves the slaughtering subject unnamed and says “the Passover”; BSB names the Levites and supplies “lamb.”
The Hebrew explicitly describes joining them when separating from the peoples’ impurity; BSB does not separately express that joining.
Close to the Hebrew.
